meta.title: Overtaking and passing oncoming vehicles
meta.summary: You will learn what to check before overtaking, which side to overtake on, where overtaking is prohibited, how to behave when you are being overtaken, and who gives way when passing oncoming vehicles on a narrow road and on a gradient.

p: Overtaking is passing one or more moving vehicles ahead, which involves leaving the lane you occupy and then returning to the lane you occupied before. If you simply drive faster than a vehicle in the adjacent lane going in the same direction and do not change lanes, that is passing, not overtaking.
Overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane is one of the most dangerous manoeuvres: misjudging the distance ends in a head-on collision. That is why the rules here are strict.

If a broken-down vehicle or another stationary object in the lane prevents you from continuing along that lane, it is an obstruction, and you are driving around it, not overtaking. A traffic jam and a vehicle that has stopped in accordance with the Rules (for example, in a queue) do not count as obstructions.

list: The lane you are moving into is clear for a sufficient distance, and you will not impede oncoming traffic or vehicles coming up behind in that lane, including those giving warning signals.
The vehicle behind you in your lane has not yet started overtaking.
The driver ahead of you in your lane has not signalled a left turn.
After overtaking, you will be able to return to your lane without impeding the vehicle you have overtaken.
lesson.tip: If even one of these conditions is not met, you must not start overtaking.

lesson.h: Which side to overtake on and where to return
p: Trackless vehicles are overtaken on the left. Exception: if the driver ahead has signalled a left turn and has already started the manoeuvre, you overtake that vehicle on the right.
When you have finished overtaking that involved moving into the oncoming lane, you must return to the lane you were driving in before.

list: At controlled intersections, if it involves moving into the oncoming lane.
At uncontrolled intersections, if you are driving on a main road that changes direction (except for permitted overtaking on the right).
At uncontrolled intersections, if you are driving on a minor road. Exceptions: roundabouts, overtaking two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar, and permitted overtaking on the right.
On pedestrian crossings, if there are pedestrians on them.
On level crossings and less than 100 m before them.
If the vehicle ahead is itself overtaking or driving around an obstruction.
At the end of an ascent and on other sections with a restricted view, if it involves moving into the oncoming lane.
On sections marked with signs 3.20 “No overtaking” and 3.22 “No overtaking by trucks” (more on this below).
lesson.tip: Under the Rules, a restricted view means the driver can see the road ahead for less than 100 m.

list: 3.20 “No overtaking”: you must not overtake anyone except single vehicles travelling slower than 30 km/h.
3.22 “No overtaking by trucks”: the same prohibition for trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t. In its zone, tractors may overtake only horse-drawn carts and bicycles.

The zone of signs 3.20 and 3.22 extends to the nearest intersection after the sign, and in a built-up area with no intersections, to the end of the built-up area. Exits from adjacent areas do not count as intersections.
The prohibition is ended by signs 3.21 and 3.23, sign 3.31 “End of all restrictions” or plate 7.2.1 “Zone of application”.
lesson.tip: If you cannot complete overtaking before sign 3.20, do not start it.

lesson.h: Road markings: where you may move into the oncoming lane
list: You must not cross solid line 1.1 or double line 1.3. Exception: you may cross line 1.1 to drive around an obstruction if there is no other way to drive around it.

Broken lines 1.5-1.8 may be crossed from either side. Approach line 1.6 (long dashes, short gaps) warns that solid line 1.1 or line 1.11 will begin soon: judge whether you will have time to complete overtaking.
Line 1.11 may be crossed from the broken-line side, and from the solid-line side only to complete overtaking or driving around an obstruction.

On a two-lane road where opposing traffic flows are separated by line 1.1 and/or sign 3.20 is in place, you must not move onto the side of the road intended for oncoming traffic, except in cases provided for by the Rules.

On roads with four or more lanes, moving onto the side of the road intended for oncoming traffic is prohibited, and on a three-lane road you must not move into the leftmost lane intended for oncoming traffic.
lesson.tip: When returning after overtaking, you may cross line 1.11 from either side, but you must not cross solid line 1.1.

lesson.h: Signalling to overtake, and overtaking without using the oncoming lane
p: Outside built-up areas, you may use the horn to warn of your intention to overtake. The light signal for this is briefly switching the headlights on and off in daytime, and switching from dipped to main-beam headlights at night.

The prohibitions at controlled intersections, at the end of an ascent and on sections with a restricted view apply to overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane. Overtaking in a clear lane of your own direction is not prohibited there by these provisions.
But at an intersection you must not pass vehicles travelling in the same direction that restrict your view, such as a bus or a truck ⟦13⟧.
A driver who is being overtaken must not hinder the overtaking by speeding up or in any other way. The sooner the overtaking vehicle returns to its lane, the safer it is for everyone.

Outside built-up areas, the driver of a slow-moving or oversized vehicle that is difficult to overtake must move as far to the right as possible and, if necessary, stop to let the vehicles queuing behind pass.

Outside built-up areas on two-lane roads, drivers of vehicles longer than 7 m and of vehicles for which a speed limit is set keep such a distance from the vehicle ahead that overtaking vehicles can return to their lane in front of them ⟦14⟧.

lesson.h: Passing oncoming vehicles on a narrow road
p: If it is difficult to pass an oncoming vehicle, first look at signs 2.6 “Priority to oncoming traffic” and 2.7 “Priority over oncoming traffic”. They tell you directly who goes first.
If there are no such signs, the driver on whose side the obstruction is must give way.

Giving way means not starting a manoeuvre if it would force the oncoming driver to change speed or direction. If the oncoming vehicle is still far away and driving around the obstruction will not impede it, you may do so.

lesson.h: Passing oncoming vehicles on a steep gradient
p: On gradients marked with signs 1.13 “Steep descent” and 1.14 “Steep ascent”, a special rule applies: if there is an obstruction, the driver going downhill gives way.
The logic is simple: for a vehicle going uphill, stopping and then moving off again is much harder and more dangerous than for a vehicle going downhill.
This rule applies only on gradients marked with signs 1.13 and 1.14. On a gradient without these signs, the driver on whose side the obstruction is gives way.
lesson.tip: Remember: on a steep gradient, the driver going downhill gives way.

keyFacts: Overtaking is passing a moving vehicle ahead, which involves leaving the lane you occupy and then returning to the lane you occupied before ⟦1⟧
Before overtaking: the lane is clear for a sufficient distance, no one behind has started overtaking, the vehicle ahead has not signalled a left turn, and you will be able to return safely ⟦2⟧
Trackless vehicles are overtaken on the left; a vehicle that has signalled a left turn and started the manoeuvre is overtaken on the right ⟦3⟧
After overtaking that involved moving into the oncoming lane, return to the lane you occupied before ⟦4⟧
The driver being overtaken must not hinder the overtaking by increasing speed or by any other actions ⟦5⟧
Overtaking is prohibited on level crossings and less than 100 m before them ⟦6⟧
Overtaking is prohibited on pedestrian crossings when there are pedestrians on them ⟦7⟧
You must not overtake a vehicle that is itself overtaking or driving around an obstruction ⟦8⟧
Overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane is prohibited at controlled intersections, at the end of an ascent and on sections with a restricted view ⟦9⟧
Outside built-up areas, a slow-moving or oversized vehicle that is difficult to overtake moves to the right and, if necessary, stops to let vehicles pass ⟦10⟧

Without signs 2.6 and 2.7, when passing oncoming vehicles is difficult, the driver on whose side the obstruction is gives way; on gradients with signs 1.13 and 1.14, the driver going downhill gives way ⟦11⟧
In the zone of sign 3.20, you may overtake only single vehicles travelling slower than 30 km/h; sign 3.22 introduces the same prohibition for trucks over 3.5 t ⟦12⟧
mistakes: Thinking that any driving faster than the adjacent lane is overtaking. Overtaking always involves leaving your lane; otherwise it is passing.
Starting to overtake without checking the mirror. If the vehicle behind has already started overtaking, you must not start.
Thinking that near a level crossing overtaking is prohibited only on the tracks themselves. The prohibition starts 100 m before the crossing.
Speeding up when you are being overtaken. This is expressly prohibited.
Thinking that on a steep gradient the driver with the obstruction on their side always gives way. On gradients with signs 1.13 and 1.14, the driver going downhill gives way.
Overtaking a vehicle that is itself overtaking. This is prohibited: three vehicles end up side by side on the road, one of them in the oncoming lane.

questions.q: You are driving behind a truck and intend to overtake it. The truck driver has switched on the left direction indicator. What should you do?
options: Quickly overtake it on the left before it starts the manoeuvre
Sound the horn and overtake it in the oncoming lane
Flash your headlights so that the driver lets you through
Do not start overtaking on the left; let it make its manoeuvre
questions.explain: Before overtaking, the driver must make sure that the vehicle ahead in the same lane has not signalled a left turn. If it has, you must not start overtaking on the left.

questions.q: The car ahead has signalled a left turn and has already started turning. On which side may you overtake it?
options: Only on the left, in the oncoming lane
On the right
Overtaking such a car is prohibited
questions.explain: Trackless vehicles are overtaken on the left, but if the driver has signalled a left turn and started the manoeuvre, the vehicle is overtaken on the right.

questions.q: Another car starts to overtake you. What must you do?
options: Speed up so that the driver realises overtaking is dangerous
Move closer to the middle of the road
Do not speed up or hinder the overtaking in any way
questions.explain: The driver of a vehicle being overtaken must not hinder the overtaking by increasing speed or by any other actions.

questions.q: You are approaching a level crossing behind a slow car. From what distance before the crossing is overtaking already prohibited?
options: Closer than 100 m
Closer than 50 m
Closer than 150 m
Closer than 300 m
questions.explain: Overtaking is prohibited on level crossings and less than 100 m before them.

questions.q: You are approaching an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing behind a slow vehicle. In which case does para. 81 expressly prohibit overtaking on the crossing itself?
options: Only during the hours of darkness
Only if the crossing is controlled
If there are pedestrians on the crossing
The Rules contain no such prohibition
questions.explain: Overtaking is prohibited on pedestrian crossings when there are pedestrians on them. Signs and solid markings may prohibit overtaking in other cases too.

questions.q: At a controlled intersection the light is green, and a motorcycle without a sidecar is moving slowly ahead of you. May you overtake it by moving into the oncoming lane right at the intersection?
options: No: such overtaking is prohibited at a controlled intersection
Yes: two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar may be overtaken at intersections
Yes, if there are no oncoming cars at the intersection
questions.explain: The intersection is controlled, and at controlled intersections overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane is prohibited, whoever you are overtaking. The exception for two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar applies only at uncontrolled intersections when you are driving on a minor road.

questions.q: You are driving on a minor road and approaching an uncontrolled intersection that is not a roundabout. A motorcycle with a sidecar is moving slowly ahead. There is no crossing traffic. May you overtake it at the intersection?
options: Yes: overtaking motorcycles at such an intersection is permitted
No: the exception is only for two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar
Yes, if the motorcycle is travelling slower than 30 km/h
questions.explain: When you are driving on a minor road, overtaking at an uncontrolled intersection is prohibited. An exception is made for two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar, and a motorcycle with a sidecar does not qualify.

questions.q: The blue car ahead of you has started to overtake a truck, as shown in the diagram. You want to overtake both at once. May you do so?
options: Yes, if the oncoming lane is clear
Yes, if you sound the horn
Yes, but only outside a built-up area
No: the car is itself overtaking
questions.explain: The blue car is itself overtaking the truck, and overtaking a vehicle that is overtaking or driving around an obstruction is prohibited: there would be three vehicles side by side on the road.

questions.q: You are driving uphill behind a single tractor travelling at about 20 km/h. There are signs on the ascent, as shown in the diagram. The crest is a few dozen metres away, and you cannot see what is beyond it. May you overtake the tractor by moving into the oncoming lane?
options: Yes: sign 3.20 allows overtaking single vehicles slower than 30 km/h
Yes, if you sound the horn before the crest
No: such overtaking is prohibited at the end of an ascent
questions.explain: It is true that sign 3.20 does not prohibit overtaking a single tractor travelling slower than 30 km/h. But at the end of an ascent and on other sections with a restricted view, overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane is prohibited: an oncoming vehicle cannot be seen beyond the crest.

questions.q: You are driving a slow-moving tractor on a narrow road outside a built-up area. It is difficult to overtake you, and a queue has built up behind. What must you do?
options: Move over to the right and, if necessary, stop to let the vehicles pass
Carry on: whether to overtake is up to the drivers behind
Switch on the hazard warning lights and drive in the middle of the lane
Switch on the left indicator so that no one behind starts overtaking
questions.explain: You are driving a slow-moving vehicle outside a built-up area, and it is difficult to overtake you. In this case, the driver moves as far to the right as possible and, if necessary, stops to let the vehicles queuing behind pass.

questions.q: On a narrow road, a broken-down truck is standing in your lane. A car is coming towards you, and it is difficult to pass each other. There are no signs 2.6 or 2.7. Who must give way?
options: The oncoming driver
Whoever reached the obstruction later
Whoever has the bigger vehicle
You: the obstruction is on your side
questions.explain: If passing oncoming vehicles is difficult and the order of passage is not set by signs 2.6 and 2.7, the driver on whose side the obstruction is must give way.

questions.q: You are driving down a steep gradient marked with signs 1.13 and 1.14. There is an obstruction in the lane of the oncoming driver, who is going uphill. It is difficult to pass each other. Who gives way?
options: The driver going uphill, as the obstruction is on their side
You, as you are going downhill
Whoever sounded the horn first
questions.explain: On gradients marked with signs 1.13 and 1.14, if there is an obstruction, the driver of the vehicle going downhill gives way.

questions.q: You want to overtake a tractor. Ahead, the broken centre line changes to an approach line and then to a solid line. On which path may you overtake?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: On path A, you return to your lane across broken approach line 1.6. Path B returns across solid line 1.1, which must not be crossed. Line 1.6 is there precisely to warn you that a solid line will begin soon.

questions.q: You are driving behind a tractor. The solid centre line will soon change to a broken one. On which path may you start overtaking now?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Both paths start by crossing solid line 1.1, which must not be crossed. You may start overtaking only where the line is already broken.

questions.q: Opposing traffic flows are separated by line 1.11, as shown in the diagram. You are in the red car and want to overtake a tractor, and the driver of the blue car wants to overtake a tractor coming the other way. Which overtaking path do the road markings permit?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Line 1.11 may be crossed from the broken-line side, and from the solid-line side only to complete overtaking or driving around an obstruction. Here the broken part is on the side of your lane: you (A) may start overtaking, but the driver of the blue car (B) may not.

questions.q: Opposing traffic flows are separated by line 1.11, as shown in the diagram. You are in the red car and want to overtake a tractor, and the driver of the blue car wants to overtake a tractor coming the other way. Which overtaking path do the road markings permit?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Now the broken part of line 1.11 is on the side of the oncoming lane. The driver of the blue car (B) may start overtaking across it, but you must not start overtaking from the solid-line side.

questions.q: You are overtaking a tractor by moving into the oncoming lane. On which path must you perform this manoeuvre?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: On completing overtaking that involved moving into the oncoming lane, the driver returns to the lane they occupied before: this is path B. You must not continue in the oncoming lane (A).

questions.q: The driver of the white car has switched on the left direction indicator and started turning left. On which path may you continue?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: You must not overtake on the left a vehicle that has signalled a left turn (B). If it has already started the manoeuvre, it is overtaken on the right, so you continue straight on in your lane (A).

questions.q: There is a pedestrian crossing ahead, and pedestrians are walking across it. You want to overtake a tractor. On which path may you overtake?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Path A goes over the pedestrian crossing while there are pedestrians on it, and overtaking is prohibited there. On path B, overtaking is completed before the crossing, after which you must give way to the pedestrians.

questions.q: There is a pedestrian crossing ahead, with no pedestrians on it or near it. You want to overtake a tractor. On which path may you overtake?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Under para. 81, overtaking on a pedestrian crossing is prohibited only when there are pedestrians on it. The crossing is empty and the centre line is broken, so both paths are permitted. As you approach the crossing, still be ready to let a pedestrian cross.

questions.q: There is a level crossing ahead; the last 100 m before it are marked in the diagram. You want to overtake a tractor. On which path may you do this?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Overtaking is prohibited on level crossings and less than 100 m before them. Path A ends before this zone, while on path B you are still in the oncoming lane within the last 100 m before the crossing.

questions.q: There is a level crossing ahead; the last 100 m before it are marked in the diagram. You want to overtake a tractor. On which path may you do this?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Both paths end before the start of the 100 m zone in front of the crossing where overtaking is prohibited. There are no other prohibitions here, so you may overtake on either of them.

questions.q: You are driving on a minor road towards an uncontrolled intersection. There is a tractor ahead. On which path may you overtake it?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: When you are driving on a minor road, overtaking at an uncontrolled intersection is prohibited (except for two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar, roundabouts and permitted overtaking on the right). Path B ends before the intersection, while on path A you overtake at the intersection itself.

questions.q: You are driving on a minor road towards an uncontrolled intersection. A motorcycle without a sidecar is moving slowly ahead. On which path may you overtake it?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Overtaking two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar is an exception to the prohibition on overtaking at an uncontrolled intersection when driving on a minor road. So both paths are permitted here.

questions.q: You are driving on a main road that goes straight through an uncontrolled intersection. A passenger car is moving slowly ahead. On which path may you overtake it?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: On a main road that does not change direction, overtaking at an uncontrolled intersection is not prohibited. The passenger car does not block your view, so both paths are suitable if the oncoming lane is clear.

questions.q: There is a controlled intersection ahead, and the light is green for you. You want to overtake a tractor. On which path may you do this?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: At controlled intersections, overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane is prohibited. Path A ends before the intersection, while on path B you enter the intersection in the oncoming lane.

questions.q: A broken-down car is standing in your lane, and it cannot be driven around without crossing the solid line. There is no oncoming traffic. On which path may you continue?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: As an exception, solid line 1.1 may be crossed to drive around an obstruction if there is no other way to drive around it: this is path B. You must not stay on the oncoming side after driving around it (A).

questions.q: You are driving down a steep descent marked with a sign, as shown in the diagram. A broken-down car is standing in your lane, and a green car is coming up from below. It is difficult to pass each other. On which path must you continue?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: On a gradient with sign 1.13, when there is an obstruction, the driver going downhill gives way, that is, you. Besides, the obstruction is on your side. Driving around it on path A would force the green car to brake, so you must stop before the obstruction (B) and let the green car pass.

questions.q: You want to overtake a tractor. The road markings ahead change as shown in the diagram: a broken line, then line 1.11, then a solid line. On which path may you overtake?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: On path B, you return across line 1.11 from its solid side: this is permitted because you are completing overtaking. On path A, you would return across solid line 1.1, which must not be crossed.

questions.q: You want to overtake a tractor. Ahead, the broken centre line changes to line 1.11, as shown in the diagram. On which path may you overtake?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Both paths start across the broken line. On path B, you return across line 1.11 from its broken side, which is permitted. So both paths are suitable.

questions.q: There is a sign ahead, as shown in the diagram. The motorcycle in front of you is travelling at about 50 km/h. On which path may you overtake it?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Sign 3.20 prohibits overtaking in its zone, except for single vehicles travelling slower than 30 km/h. The motorcycle is going faster, so overtaking must be completed before the sign, as on path B. Path A continues into the zone of the sign.

questions.q: You have already driven past the “No overtaking” sign, and ahead is the sign that ends its zone, as shown in the diagram. The motorcycle in front of you is travelling at about 50 km/h. On which path may you start overtaking it now?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: You are in the zone of sign 3.20, the motorcycle is travelling faster than 30 km/h, and both paths start before sign 3.21. You may start overtaking only after sign 3.21 “End of no-overtaking zone”.

questions.q: The white car ahead of you in the left lane has switched on its left direction indicator and started turning at the intersection. You are behind it and going straight on. On which path may you continue?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: A vehicle that has signalled a left turn and started the manoeuvre is overtaken on the right: you change to the right lane and go straight on (A). Path B leads across the double solid line onto the oncoming side of a four-lane road, which is prohibited, as is overtaking a left-turning vehicle on the left.

questions.q: There is a dangerous bend ahead where the road is visible for less than 100 m. The bend starts at the label in the diagram; before it, the road is clearly visible. You want to overtake a tractor. On which path may you do this?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: On sections with a restricted view (less than 100 m), overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane is prohibited. On path B, overtaking is completed before the bend, while on path A you enter the bend still in the oncoming lane.

questions.q: You are driving in town in the left lane behind a slow white car. The right lane is clear. On which path may you continue?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Path A crosses double solid line 1.3 and leads onto the oncoming side of a four-lane road, which is not allowed. You may change to the right lane and drive on in the clear lane (B): driving in a lane faster than the adjacent one does not count as overtaking.

questions.q: You are driving uphill behind a tractor. The diagram marks the crest of the hill and the last 100 m before it; oncoming vehicles cannot be seen beyond the crest. On which path may you overtake the tractor?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: At the end of an ascent, overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane is prohibited: you cannot see who is coming beyond the crest. Path A ends before this section, while on path B you would be in the oncoming lane right before the crest.

questions.q: You are driving a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 15 t and have driven past the sign shown in the diagram. A single tractor ahead is travelling at about 20 km/h. On which path may you overtake it?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Sign 3.22 prohibits trucks over 3.5 t from overtaking, except for overtaking single vehicles travelling slower than 30 km/h. The tractor is travelling at 20 km/h, so you may overtake on either path if the oncoming lane is clear.

questions.q: You want to overtake a truck, and a green car is approaching from the opposite direction, as shown in the diagram. May you start overtaking?
options: No: the oncoming car is too close
Yes, if you accelerate hard and return quickly
Yes, if you flash your headlights at the oncoming car
Yes: the line is broken, so overtaking is permitted here
questions.explain: Before overtaking, you must make sure that the lane you are moving into is clear for a sufficient distance and that you will not impede oncoming traffic. The green car is too close, so you must not start overtaking.

questions.q: You want to overtake a truck, but the blue car behind you has already started overtaking, as shown in the diagram. What should you do?
options: Do not start overtaking until it has overtaken you
Start overtaking at the same time, keeping to the right
Move to the left so that it cannot overtake
Brake sharply so that it gets past sooner
questions.explain: Before starting to overtake, the driver makes sure that the vehicle behind in the same lane has not started overtaking. The blue car has already moved into the oncoming lane, so you need to wait and not hinder it.

questions.q: Ahead, trucks are travelling in a line with small gaps between them. You want to overtake the truck nearest to you, as shown by the arrow. May you do so?
options: Yes: the oncoming lane is clear and there is no oncoming traffic
Yes, if you then stay in the oncoming lane until you have overtaken them all
No: there will be no room to return to your lane
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
questions.explain: Before overtaking, you must make sure that when you finish you will be able to return to your lane without impeding the vehicle being overtaken. There is almost no space between the trucks, so there will be nowhere to return to.

questions.q: You want to overtake a truck using the left lane. A blue car is quickly approaching from behind in that lane and flashing its headlights. May you change to the left lane now?
options: Yes: you have switched on your direction indicator
Yes, if you accelerate hard straight away
No: you would impede the blue car
Yes, as there is no one ahead in that lane
questions.explain: When moving into another lane to overtake, you must not impede vehicles coming up behind in that lane, including those giving warning signals. Let the blue car pass, then start overtaking.

questions.q: A blue truck is overtaking you, and a green car is approaching it from the opposite direction, as shown in the diagram. What is the best thing for you to do?
options: Speed up so that the truck abandons the overtaking
Move towards the centre line so that the truck cannot return in front of you
Do not accelerate and, if necessary, slow down
Switch on the hazard warning lights and carry on as before
questions.explain: The driver being overtaken must not hinder the overtaking by increasing speed or by other actions. There is a risk of a head-on collision, so it is sensible to reduce speed and help the truck return to its lane sooner.

questions.q: You are driving an oversized road train on a narrow road outside a built-up area. It is difficult to overtake you, and a queue of vehicles has built up behind. What must you do?
options: Carry on: whether to overtake is up to the other drivers
Switch on the left indicator so that the vehicles behind do not overtake
Drive in the middle of the road so that no one tries to overtake
Move over to the right and, if necessary, stop
questions.explain: Outside built-up areas, the driver of a slow-moving or oversized vehicle that is difficult to overtake moves as far to the right as possible and, if necessary, stops to let the vehicles queuing behind pass.

questions.q: The blue car ahead is driving around a broken-down car, as shown in the diagram. May you overtake the blue car at this moment?
options: Yes, provided the oncoming lane is clear
Yes, if you sound the horn first
Yes, but only on the right-hand side
No: it is driving around an obstruction
questions.explain: Overtaking a vehicle that is overtaking or driving around an obstruction is prohibited. The blue car has already moved to the left to drive around the obstruction, so you must not overtake it at this moment.

questions.q: There is a dangerous bend ahead, and the road is visible for about 60 m. You want to overtake a truck, as shown by the arrow. May you do this?
options: Yes, if no oncoming vehicles are visible
Yes, if you sound the horn before the bend
Yes, if the truck is travelling slower than 30 km/h
No: the view is restricted here
questions.explain: A restricted view means the road is visible for less than 100 m in the direction of travel. On such sections, overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane is prohibited: an oncoming vehicle may appear suddenly.

questions.q: There is a dangerous bend ahead, and the road is visible for about 60 m. There are two lanes in your direction, and the left one is clear. May you overtake the truck in the left lane of your direction, as shown by the arrow?
options: Yes: only overtaking via the oncoming lane is prohibited
No: any overtaking is prohibited where the view is restricted
Yes, but only if the truck signals a right turn
No: overtaking is always prohibited on a four-lane road
questions.explain: On sections with a restricted view, the Rules prohibit overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane. Overtaking in the left lane of your own direction is not prohibited by this provision.

questions.q: You have driven past the sign shown in the diagram. A single truck ahead is travelling at about 20 km/h. May you overtake it on the path shown if the oncoming lane is clear and there are no other prohibitions?
options: Yes: a single vehicle slower than 30 km/h may be overtaken
No: in the zone of sign 3.20, overtaking any vehicle is prohibited
Yes, but only with the hazard warning lights on
No: the truck may only be driven around on the shoulder
questions.explain: Sign 3.20 “No overtaking” prohibits overtaking all vehicles except single vehicles travelling at less than 30 km/h. The truck is travelling at about 20 km/h, so it may be overtaken if there are no other prohibitions.

questions.q: You have driven past the sign shown in the diagram. A passenger car ahead is travelling at about 50 km/h. May you overtake it on the path shown if the oncoming lane is clear?
options: Yes, if you complete the overtaking quickly
Yes, if you sound the horn
No: it is travelling faster than 30 km/h
No: only trucks may be overtaken in the zone of this sign
questions.explain: The car is travelling at 50 km/h, so the exception for single vehicles slower than 30 km/h does not apply to it. In the zone of sign 3.20, overtaking it is prohibited.

questions.q: You have driven past the “No overtaking” sign and then through an intersection, as shown in the diagram. There were no other signs. May you overtake the truck now?
options: Yes: the zone of sign 3.20 ended at the intersection
No: the prohibition applies until sign 3.21
No: the prohibition applies until the end of the road
Yes, but only if the truck is travelling slower than 30 km/h
questions.explain: The zone of sign 3.20 extends to the nearest intersection after the sign. After the intersection, the prohibition no longer applies, and you may overtake, following the other rules.

questions.q: You are driving a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 12 t and have driven past the sign shown in the diagram. A passenger car ahead is travelling at about 60 km/h. May you overtake it?
options: Yes, if the oncoming lane is clear
Yes: the sign only prohibits overtaking trucks
No: the sign prohibits trucks from moving at all
No: the car is travelling faster than 30 km/h
questions.explain: Sign 3.22 “No overtaking by trucks” applies to trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t. They are prohibited from overtaking all vehicles except single vehicles travelling slower than 30 km/h.

questions.q: You are in a passenger car and have driven past the sign shown in the diagram. There is a truck ahead. May you overtake it if the oncoming lane is clear and there are no other prohibitions?
options: No: the sign prohibits overtaking trucks
No: the sign prohibits all overtaking
Yes: the sign does not apply to cars
Yes, but only after sign 3.21
questions.explain: Sign 3.22 prohibits overtaking by trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t. It does not apply to a passenger car, so you may overtake the truck, following the other rules.

questions.q: On a narrow road, a broken-down car is standing in the lane of the oncoming green car. There are no priority signs, and it is difficult to pass each other. Who goes through this spot first?
options: The green car
You
Whoever sounds the horn first
Whoever has the bigger vehicle
questions.explain: If passing oncoming vehicles is difficult and there are no signs 2.6 and 2.7, the driver on whose side the obstruction is gives way. The obstruction is on the green car’s side, so you go first.

questions.q: Before a narrow section, the sign shown in the diagram is placed for your direction. A broken-down car is standing in your lane, and a green car is coming towards you. It is difficult to pass each other. Who goes first?
options: The green car: the obstruction is on your side
Whoever was first to reach the obstruction
No one, until the broken-down car has been removed
You: sign 2.7 gives you priority over oncoming traffic
questions.explain: The rule “the driver on whose side the obstruction is gives way” applies only if the order of passage is not set by signs 2.6 and 2.7. Sign 2.7 “Priority over oncoming traffic” is placed for your direction, so you go first.

questions.q: Before a narrow section, the sign shown in the diagram is placed for your direction. A broken-down car is standing in the lane of the oncoming green car. It is difficult to pass each other. Who goes first?
options: The green car: you have sign 2.6
You: the obstruction is on the oncoming side
Whoever sounds the horn first
Both at the same time, each in their own lane
questions.explain: Sign 2.6 “Priority to oncoming traffic” requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles that are on the narrow section or approaching it. The order of passage is set by the sign, so the obstruction rule does not apply here.

questions.q: You are driving up a steep ascent marked with a sign, as shown in the diagram. A broken-down car is standing in your lane, and a green car is coming down from above. It is difficult to pass each other. Who goes first?
options: The green car: the obstruction is on your side
Whoever switches on the hazard warning lights first
Whoever has more passengers
You: the driver going downhill gives way
questions.explain: On gradients marked with signs 1.13 and 1.14, if there is an obstruction, the driver going downhill gives way. The green car is going downhill, so it lets you pass, even though the obstruction is on your side.

questions.q: You are driving down a gentle gradient; there are no signs 1.13 or 1.14. A broken-down car is standing in the lane of the oncoming green car, which is going uphill. It is difficult to pass each other. Who goes first?
options: You: the obstruction is on the green car’s side
The green car: the driver going downhill always gives way
Whoever reached the obstruction first
Both at the same time
questions.explain: The special rule “the driver going downhill gives way” applies on gradients marked with signs 1.13 and 1.14. There are none here, so the general rule applies: the driver on whose side the obstruction is gives way, that is, the driver of the green car.

questions.q: At the intersection, the main road turns left, as shown by the plate. You are driving along it behind a truck. May you overtake the truck on the left at this intersection?
options: No: the main road changes direction here
Yes: overtaking at an intersection is permitted on a main road
Yes, if the truck is travelling slower than 30 km/h
Yes, if you sound the horn in advance
questions.explain: The main road changes direction here, and overtaking is prohibited at such an uncontrolled intersection. The Rules make an exception only for permitted overtaking on the right.

questions.q: The traffic light at the intersection is flashing amber. You are driving straight on along the main road behind a slow passenger car. May you overtake it at the intersection, as shown by the arrow?
options: No: overtaking is always prohibited at intersections with traffic lights
Yes, but only if the car is travelling slower than 30 km/h
Yes: the intersection is uncontrolled and the main road goes straight on
No: you must stop when the amber light is flashing
questions.explain: When the amber signal is flashing, the intersection is considered uncontrolled. At an uncontrolled intersection, overtaking is prohibited for those driving on a minor road or on a main road that changes direction. You are going straight on along the main road, so overtaking is not prohibited here.

questions.q: You have started overtaking and are driving in the oncoming lane alongside a truck, but an oncoming car has appeared ahead, and you will not be able to complete the overtaking safely. What should you do?
options: Accelerate as hard as possible to complete the overtaking in time
Switch on the hazard warning lights and carry on in the oncoming lane
Pull onto the shoulder on the oncoming side
Abandon the overtaking: slow down and return behind the truck
questions.explain: When a hazard arises, the driver takes measures to reduce speed. The oncoming lane is no longer clear for a distance sufficient for overtaking, so it is safer to abandon the manoeuvre and return to your lane behind the truck.

questions.q: A blue car coming towards you starts to overtake a truck and moves into your lane, as shown in the diagram. What should you do?
options: Keep going without slowing down: you are in your own lane
Move into the oncoming lane to get past each other
Slow down, even to a stop, and keep to the right
Flash your headlights and speed up
questions.explain: An oncoming car in your lane is a hazard that you can see. You must reduce speed, even to a stop, and keep closer to the right-hand edge so that it has time to return to its lane.

questions.q: The white car ahead has stopped with its left direction indicator on and is waiting for oncoming vehicles to pass. You cannot drive around it on the right within the lane: there is not enough width. May you drive around it on the right-hand shoulder?
options: No: driving on shoulders is prohibited; you must wait
Yes: a vehicle turning left is overtaken on the right
Yes, if you switch on your right direction indicator
Yes, if the shoulder has an asphalt surface
questions.explain: A vehicle that has signalled a left turn and started the manoeuvre is overtaken on the right, but on the carriageway. Driving on the shoulders is prohibited, so if there is not enough room in the lane, you must wait.

questions.q: You have driven past the signs shown in the diagram. A truck is moving slowly ahead, and the oncoming lane is clear. May you overtake it?
options: No: the “No overtaking” sign still applies
Yes: sign 3.21 marks the end of the no-overtaking zone
Yes, but only if the truck is travelling slower than 30 km/h
No, not until the nearest intersection
questions.explain: Sign 3.21 “End of no-overtaking zone” cancels sign 3.20. From there on, you may overtake, following the other rules.

questions.q: You are driving in the zone of the “No overtaking” sign. Which of the signs shown cancels this prohibition?
options: A
B
C
questions.explain: Sign 3.31 “End of all restrictions” (B) ends the zone of several signs at once, including 3.20. Sign 3.25 (A) cancels only the speed limit, and 3.23 (C) only the no-overtaking rule for trucks.

questions.q: A broken-down car is standing in your lane. The oncoming green car is still far away. May you drive around the obstruction now, as shown by the arrow?
options: No: the obstruction is on your side, so you must wait until the oncoming car has passed
Yes, but only after sounding the horn
No: driving around an obstruction via the oncoming lane is always prohibited
Yes, if this will not force the oncoming driver to change speed or direction
questions.explain: Giving way means not making a manoeuvre if it would force a road user who has priority to change direction or speed. If the oncoming car is far away and driving around the obstruction will not impede it, you may do so.

questions.q: The driver of the white car ahead has switched on the right direction indicator to turn into a yard. Does this prohibit you from overtaking it on the left?
options: Yes: you must not overtake a vehicle with any indicator on
Yes, if the yard is less than 100 m away
No: the prohibition concerns only a left-turn signal
No, but you may only overtake it on the right
questions.explain: Before overtaking, you must make sure that the driver ahead has not signalled a manoeuvre to the left. A right indicator does not in itself prohibit overtaking on the left, but the lane must be clear and you must not impede that driver’s manoeuvre.

questions.q: You are approaching a controlled intersection, and the light is green. May you overtake a slow white car in the left lane of your direction, as shown by the arrow, without moving onto the oncoming side of the road?
options: No: overtaking is always prohibited at controlled intersections
Yes: only overtaking via the oncoming lane is prohibited
Yes, but only if the car ahead is stationary
No: you may overtake only up to the stop line
questions.explain: At controlled intersections, the Rules prohibit overtaking that involves moving into the oncoming lane, while overtaking in a lane of your own direction is not prohibited by this provision. But at an intersection you must not pass vehicles that block your view, such as a bus ⟦15⟧.

questions.q: Where must the driver of a slow-moving or oversized vehicle that is difficult to overtake let the vehicles queuing behind pass?
options: Outside built-up areas
Only on motorways
Only in built-up areas
Only on roads with a central reservation
questions.explain: The rule in para. 82 concerns driving outside built-up areas: there, the driver of a slow-moving or oversized vehicle moves as far to the right as possible and, if necessary, stops to let the vehicles queuing behind pass.

questions.q: You are driving a truck with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t. Whom are you allowed to overtake in the zone of this sign?
options: No one
Only passenger cars
Single vehicles travelling slower than 30 km/h
Any vehicle, if the oncoming lane is clear
questions.explain: Sign 3.22 “No overtaking by trucks” prohibits trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t from overtaking all vehicles except single vehicles travelling at less than 30 km/h.

questions.q: You are driving a tractor in the zone of this sign. Whom are you allowed to overtake?
options: Any vehicles travelling slower than 30 km/h
No one
Only motorcycles
Only horse-drawn carts and bicycles
questions.explain: Sign 3.22 applies not only to trucks over 3.5 t: in its zone, tractors are prohibited from overtaking all vehicles except horse-drawn carts and bicycles.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an obstruction to traffic under the Rules?
options: A broken-down car standing in the lane
A tree that has fallen into the lane
A traffic jam (tailback) in the lane
A concrete block lying in the lane
questions.explain: An obstruction is a stationary object in a lane that prevents you from continuing along that lane. A traffic jam and a vehicle that has stopped in the lane as required by the Rules (for example, in a queue) do not count as obstructions.

questions.q: You are driving on a minor road. At which intersection do the Rules not prohibit you from overtaking?
options: At any uncontrolled intersection
At a roundabout
At a controlled intersection, by moving into the oncoming lane
Overtaking at intersections is always prohibited
questions.explain: When you are driving on a minor road, overtaking at an uncontrolled intersection is prohibited, but there are exceptions: roundabouts, overtaking two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar, and permitted overtaking on the right.

questions.q: You are driving in the right lane faster than a blue car moving in the left lane in the same direction, and you do not change lanes. What is this manoeuvre called?
options: Overtaking
Driving around an obstruction
Changing lanes
Passing
questions.explain: Passing means moving faster than vehicles in the adjacent lane going in the same direction. Overtaking always involves leaving your lane and returning to it, and driving in a lane faster than the adjacent one does not count as overtaking.

questions.q: When is the view of the road considered restricted under the Rules?
options: When the road ahead is visible for less than 100 m
When the road is visible for less than 300 m in fog or rain
Only during the hours of darkness on an unlit road
When sign 1.11.1 “Dangerous bend to the right” stands before the section
questions.explain: A restricted view means the road is visible for less than 100 m in the direction of travel because of terrain, bends in the road, vegetation, buildings or other objects, including vehicles. Visibility of less than 300 m in fog, rain, snowfall or at twilight is called poor visibility.

questions.q: Outside a built-up area, how may you warn the driver ahead of your intention to overtake?
options: By briefly switching on the hazard warning lights
By switching on the right direction indicator
With the horn or by flashing the headlights
You may not: the Rules prohibit signals when overtaking
questions.explain: Outside built-up areas, you may use the horn to warn of your intention to overtake. The light signal for this is repeatedly switching the headlights on and off for short periods in daytime, and repeatedly switching from dipped to main-beam headlights at night.

questions.q: Which of the following do the Rules NOT require you to check before starting to overtake?
options: That the lane for overtaking is clear for a sufficient distance
That no one behind you in your lane has started overtaking
That the vehicle being overtaken has its dipped headlights on
That after overtaking you can return to your lane without impeding the vehicle overtaken
questions.explain: Before overtaking, you must make sure that the lane is clear for a sufficient distance, no one behind has started overtaking, the driver ahead has not signalled a left turn, and you will be able to return safely. The headlights of the vehicle being overtaken are not on this list.

questions.q: You are driving a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 10 t and have driven past this sign. What does it mean for you?
options: End of the zone where overtaking by trucks is prohibited
Start of the zone where overtaking by trucks is prohibited
End of the speed limit zone for trucks
Prohibition of truck traffic
questions.explain: Sign 3.23 ends the zone of sign 3.22 “No overtaking by trucks”. After it, a truck may overtake again, following the general rules.

questions.q: You are driving around a car that has broken down and is standing in your lane, as shown in the diagram. Is this manoeuvre overtaking?
options: Yes: any driving in the oncoming lane is overtaking
No: this is driving around a stationary obstruction
Yes, if the manoeuvre crosses a broken line
No, this is passing
questions.explain: Overtaking is passing a moving vehicle ahead by leaving your lane. The broken-down car is stationary and prevents you from driving along the lane: it is an obstruction, and you are driving around it.
